races.name: Behind The Lens Media Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: The Fixer
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse who needs a strong pace to reel in rivals; trainer Scott Dixon's 1/22 14-day record is unremarkable, 53 days off the track is a notable absence, and recent form figures of 0-0-0 at this track and trip on Standard offer little encouragement on Good ground.
runners_data.comment: A winner two starts back gives The Fixer a recent form boost, though he was beaten into eighth last time out and hasn't run for 53 days; with a struggling yard sending him out at just 5% over the past fortnight, confidence in him resuming that winning thread is tempered.

runners_data.name: Little Jaybee
runners_data.note: David Evans has strong recent form (1/8 in 14 days) and this 3yo has placed twice at 5f on Good, making him the most course-going-fit of the closers; Joe Leavy takes the ride and his sim-going record of 2P from 11 runs on comparable ground suggests he runs his race without winning.
runners_data.comment: Little Jaybee shaped with promise on her two most recent starts, finishing third in each, and returns on a quick turnaround of just 16 days with experience of today's trip and going in her favour; yet to win in recent starts, but our rating of 71 marks her out as the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Son Of Astar
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll sends this one out 35 days fresh with David Probert booked, a combination that often signals intent; a genuine hold-up type whose natural style is racing from the rear — in a field this packed with closers he is unlikely to get the clear run he needs, and his sim-going strike rate of 1W from 15 on Good tempers enthusiasm.
runners_data.comment: Son Of Astar shaped with promise when second three starts back, and he has run over today's trip and going, with our rating of 60 suggesting he holds strong claims against this field; the concern is a winless run of recent form and that 133 lb burden.

runners_data.name: Forever Glamorous
runners_data.note: Christopher Mason's filly has won at 5f on Good and placed at 3f and 6f, giving her genuine versatility; she has form to fill in at the front end and, though her natural inclination is to close, she has the tactical speed to secure a prominent berth if Gina Mangan rides her handily — headgear noted (p).
runners_data.comment: Forever Glamorous shaped with real promise when third last time out, and a winner two starts back, giving him a solid recent profile; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 133 lb from stall three is the weight to watch.

runners_data.name: Bridget's Baby
runners_data.note: Ran just two days ago which is an aggressive return, though Tony Carroll clearly thinks she's in good form after a recent win and place at 5f on Good; apprentice Myla Coppins (5lb) keeps costs down, and while she is a natural closer, she has the proven ability at this trip and going to challenge if getting a clear run.
runners_data.comment: Bridget's Baby won two starts back and was second three starts back, but a sixth last time out on just two days' rest leaves fitness a concern; she has run over today's trip and going before, though 131 lb is a stiff ask at this level.

runners_data.name: Call Time
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner and the race's principal pace-setter; a 76-day absence is a concern and her sim-going record of 0W 1P from 15 runs on Good is modest, but with nothing to chase her she can regulate the fractions — headgear (p) noted and Taylor Fisher's low-profile booking keeps costs minimal.
runners_data.comment: Call Time has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 62 puts him among the chief dangers in this field, yet he arrives winless in his last five starts after a run of disappointing efforts, and 76 days off the track is the question his supporters must answer.

runners_data.name: Red Walls
runners_data.note: An 8yo with a deeply modest recent record (0-8-3-8-8), racing over 5f at Ffos Las on Good is a step up in conditions from his usual soft/standard outings; Ben Ffrench Davis (5) is an inexperienced partner and, as a repositioned hold-up type in a field already crowded at the rear, his chance looks slim.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Red Walls faces a stiff task here, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns in reasonable time, 18 days since his last outing.

runners_data.name: Kodi K
runners_data.note: Liam Wright (3) claims 3lb on this lightly weighted 3yo who has placed twice at 5f on Good; his form at this trip is better than his overall figures suggest and, as a horse shuffled forward by redistribution, his natural finishing style means he needs the clearest possible run — capable of a big each-way effort if the gaps open.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked seventh of eight on our figures, Kodi K faces a stiff task here, though he has run over today's distance and going before and the second two starts back at least shows he can threaten the places; drawn in stall one off 21 days, he needs more consistency.

races.paceDynamic: Call Time is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner 5f handicap at Ffos Las and, with no genuine rival to press her for the lead, she should be able to dictate at a controlled, sustainable tempo on Good turf. Behind her, the field is overwhelmingly populated by hold-up types — The Fixer, Son Of Astar, Forever Glamorous, Bridget's Baby, Red Walls and Kodi K all prefer to race from off the pace — meaning the race shape hinges almost entirely on whether Call Time's moderate, uncontested lead is catchable. This field holds more true hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear; with so many closers competing for similar ground in the straight, the runners most likely to actually secure a forward position behind Call Time are Forever Glamorous (who has placed prominently before) and Bridget's Baby (recent winner from off the pace but capable of tracking). A lone front-runner setting a comfortable pace on Good ground over 5f strongly favours runners who can sit just off the pace and produce a sustained finish, rather than deep closers who need a strong gallop to reel in a loose leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Call Time Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Call Time is allowed to bowl along at her own rhythm and the pack fails to close the gap entering the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Call Time dictates every yard at a sustainable clip, leaving hold-up horses with insufficient time to close on Good ground over this sprint trip; any runner able to sit within two lengths and quicken will be best placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Swamp Tired Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Call Time has set just enough pace to drain her late reserves and the late-challengers arrive in a wave inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A pace that is fractionally too strong for Call Time to sustain sees the field compress in the closing stages, rewarding those with the best late sectionals; genuine hold-up horses who find the best run through traffic will dominate.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse sitting second or third establishes a clear sightline on Call Time from the outset and outkicks the field in the final 100 yards.
scenarios.body: With the leader not setting a blistering pace, the horse immediately behind has the ideal viewing platform and enough gas left to accelerate when it matters; this scenario rewards class and a clean passage over raw finishing speed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic Scrimmage Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the congested hold-up group causes traffic problems throughout and the race devolves into a messy, compressed finish with no clean winner emerging from the pack.
scenarios.body: Multiple closers fighting for the same ground on the inside create interference, and only the horse with the clearest run benefits regardless of raw ability; low-weight runners with shrewd tactical jockeys are best placed.

watchPoints.text: Call Time — monitor whether she jumps cleanly and immediately takes up the lead; if she is slow away or pressed by Forever Glamorous early, the entire pace map changes and hold-up horses will find a much stronger gallop to aim at.

Forever Glamorous and Bridget's Baby — both are natural closers likely to be ridden more prominently than usual; if they fight for the same tracking position behind Call Time, they risk burning energy early and becoming easy pickings for deeper closers.

Son Of Astar and The Fixer — with six hold-up horses competing for limited daylight on a 5f track, traffic congestion in the final two furlongs is a real risk; David Probert (Son Of Astar) and Kieran O'Neill (The Fixer) will need to find gaps that may not appear until it is too late.

Red Walls — the 8yo has done all his recent running at 6f on Soft or Standard; dropping to 5f on Good ground with a 5lb apprentice is a significant ask and a weakening finish from this runner would confirm the pace was too strong for the closers to exploit.

races.name: Golwg Gwendraeth Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Bella Bisbee
runners_data.note: Recent third on Good going over 7f is exactly the profile this race needs; Kieran O'Neill rides prominently by nature and will look to track Cypriot Diaspora closely, and the 1W3P record on similar going confirms she handles these conditions well — the 13-day return is no concern.
runners_data.comment: Bella Bisbee shaped well when third last time out and a winner six starts back, and she brings experience of today's trip and going into this; the worry is a trainer firing at just 5% in the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Lerwick
runners_data.note: A hold-up operator returning after 24 days with a headgear flag (best), Callum Hutchinson will need to find daylight through a congested field; the lone win in this form string came over 8f on Good, suggesting the 7½f trip may just be on the sharp side for a closer needing time to warm up.
runners_data.comment: Lerwick comes here off a win last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, making him a serious contender, and our rating marks him as the top-ranked runner in the field; the main risk is that his four starts before that victory brought modest efforts, hinting at some inconsistency.

runners_data.name: The Stone Power
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's three-year-old won last time over 8f on Good and has been progressively campaigned; Rhys Clutterbuck takes the ride and the horse's prominent style fits the race perfectly, though the step back to 7½f from 8f-plus trips is the one question mark over his stamina profile here.
runners_data.comment: The Stone Power won last time out and has experience of today's distance and going, making him a clear threat from stall two carrying 135 lb; the solitary pull-up in recent starts is the one blot punters will need to forgive.

runners_data.name: Santiago Boy
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and has placed twice in recent starts, but both placings came at Sandown on Standard — the single Good-going run produced only a 4th and the 0W0P record on this surface type is a red flag; Harry Vigors (5lb claim) alleviates the weight but the going concern is real.
runners_data.comment: Consistent sort who has finished second in each of his last two starts and returns on a quick nine-day turnaround in good heart, having run over today's distance and going before; winless in recent starts but his profile fits these conditions well enough to make him our pick from stall one carrying 131 lb.

runners_data.name: Mountain Of Light
runners_data.note: Limited form, just three career starts, but two of those produced placing efforts on Good going over 8f; James Horton's three-year-old drops back from 9f and races prominently — if the field bunches, Stevie Donohoe will need a clear run in the straight.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts, with an eighth and seventh bracketing a runner-up finish, Mountain Of Light looks up against it from stall ten carrying 130 lb, and our rating of 69 ranks her ninth of ten; experience over today's trip and going at least counts for something.

runners_data.name: Dappled Light
runners_data.note: Adrian Wintle's six-year-old has been in red-hot form with three wins and two seconds in five runs, all on Good or similar going; a natural prominent racer whose position in the race shape reflects overcrowding at the front rather than his true inclination, and a STYLE_FIT of 0.92 confirms he is unlikely to get the lead he craves — discount accordingly, though raw form is compelling.
runners_data.comment: Dappled Light won back-to-back before consecutive runner-up efforts, showing consistency in recent starts, though 43 days off the track is a fitness question mark; he has distance and going experience to call on, but 130 lb is a testing burden from stall seven.

runners_data.name: Gelato
runners_data.note: Taryn Langley (5lb claim) aboard a hold-up type that won over 8f on Soft — the Good ground and 7½f trip are both shorter and firmer than ideal; the 24-day break is fine but Gelato's best run came under different conditions and this looks a tough spot.
runners_data.comment: Won two starts back but has been below par either side of that success, finishing fifth last time out and well beaten in three of her last five; Gelato has run over today's trip and going, carries 126 lb from stall four, and returns after 24 days off.

runners_data.name: Cypriot Diaspora
runners_data.note: Ryan Kavanagh (3lb claim) on the only confirmed front-runner in the field — Rod Millman's five-year-old has solid Good-going form (1W3P in 8 runs) and the unchallenged lead is a rare luxury; the 7-day turnaround is a potential fitness flag but recent consistency suggests the horse is in a productive spell.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Cypriot Diaspora faces a stiff ask ranked eighth of ten on our figures, though she has run over today's distance and going before and a return to form two starts back — when second — offers a slender foothold seven days on.

runners_data.name: Nebbia
runners_data.note: David Probert takes over on Hughie Morrison's three-year-old who returns after 42 days; all form has been over shorter trips (5-6f) on Standard or Good, so this step up to 7½f is a significant stamina question — the 0W1P record on Good going over sprint trips does not obviously translate to this test.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Nebbia does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and a return from 42 days off could freshen her up, though that eighth last time out is hard to ignore against this level of opposition.

runners_data.name: Grimese's Special
runners_data.note: J S Moore's three-year-old has been off 80 days, wears a hood, and is a natural hold-up horse whose redistributed position on the map reflects the field's overcrowding at the rear rather than a change of tactic; the long absence, a STYLE_FIT of 0.90, and the lowest OR in the field (56) make this a very difficult winning case — the only win came on Heavy/AW conditions at Hereford.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Grimese's Special faces a stiff task after 80 days off the track and a run of three poor efforts in her last three starts, though she has distance and going experience to call on and showed she can win in recent form.

races.paceDynamic: Cypriot Diaspora is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival for the lead, should settle into a controlled, unhurried gallop from the front on Good ground over 7½f at Ffos Las — a flat, turning track that rewards horses travelling comfortably in the first half of the race. Behind him, Bella Bisbee, The Stone Power, Santiago Boy, and Mountain Of Light all want to race prominently, creating a congested chasing pack that will jostle for position between the 2f and 3f poles, where Ffos Las tightens through the turn. That pressure from the prominent group is unlikely to be severe enough to crack Cypriot Diaspora early, but it will compress the field and create traffic dangers for those trying to pick through between 2f and 1f out. This race shape — a single unchallenged leader dictating a sustainable pace, followed by a bunched midfield — most favours hold-up horses with a clean turn of foot, provided they can find daylight in the final two furlongs, and prominent racers who can sit just off the pace without getting caught in the scramble. The field holds more prominent types than the race shape can accommodate cleanly: Dappled Light and Grimese's Special are true front-running and hold-up horses respectively who have been redistributed on the map, and of the genuine prominent cluster, Bella Bisbee and The Stone Power are most likely to actually secure the positions they want given recent form and course suitability.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cypriot Diaspora Controls Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Cypriot Diaspora gets a clean lead and the prominent pack settles rather than chasing him hard.
scenarios.body: Cypriot Diaspora dictates a measured gallop, conserves energy through the sweeping Ffos Las turn, and the compact prominent cluster behind him spends too much energy jostling to mount a coordinated challenge in the straight; the leader's advantage is never seriously threatened.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pick Him Off
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent racers immediately behind Cypriot Diaspora travel fluently and the leader's early-race control is undermined by the compression of four horses hunting him from 3f out.
scenarios.body: One or two of the handy prominent types — most likely Bella Bisbee or The Stone Power, who both have strong recent form at this trip and going — stalk the leader into the straight and overhaul him inside the final furlong as their fresher legs tell.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Find Gap
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent scramble creates a sufficiently strong mid-race pace that the field strings out and hold-up horses get a clear passage inside the final 2f.
scenarios.body: Lerwick or Nebbia, racing from the rear, finds the field beginning to fan out through the final bend and delivers a late run into a race that has burned itself out in front; however, genuine hold-up horses are limited in this field and Grimese's Special is tagged as racing out of role, reducing the likelihood of this shape producing a clear winner.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Midfielders Score
scenarios.trigger: If Cypriot Diaspora sets an unexpectedly sharp early pace under pressure and the field races beyond its comfort level, leaving midfield-mapped runners to pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: An inflated early gallop collapses the leading group in the final 2f, and horses mapped in midfield — including the redistributed Dappled Light who is a natural prominent type pushed wider — inherit the race; this scenario is discounted because the pace input evidence suggests restraint, not a burn-up.

watchPoints.text: Prominent traffic danger 2-3f out: with Bella Bisbee, The Stone Power, Santiago Boy and Mountain Of Light all pressing behind Cypriot Diaspora, Ffos Las's sweeping left-hand bend creates a genuine pocket risk — horses drawn wide or slow to react at the 2f pole could find themselves with nowhere to go.

Lerwick's headgear (best) signals the trainer expects a peak effort, but the hold-up style requires a clear split that this congested prominent group may never provide — watch for Callum Hutchinson having to switch wide, costing vital ground.

Cypriot Diaspora's 7-day turnaround after a run is worth monitoring in-running — if the leader shows any signs of laboured breathing or shortening stride entering the straight, the entire pace scenario pivots and the prominent pair immediately behind become winning favourites.

Dappled Light's recent three-timer on Good going makes him statistically the most in-form horse in the race, but the redistribution note is genuine — if he fails to press forward from the gate and gets stuck three or four wide at the turn, his winning chance diminishes sharply regardless of raw ability.

Nebbia and Grimese's Special represent the most speculative hold-up threats — both are stepping up significantly in trip relative to their best form, and if the pace is genuinely sustainable rather than strong, neither will see enough of a fade ahead of them to make up the ground they will need.

races.name: Dandara Homes Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Esplanade
runners_data.note: OR=120 filly for Charles Hills who holds a class edge on paper, but six career starts have yielded no win and only two placed efforts, and the 7f-8f form on Soft and Good shows consistency without a decisive breakthrough — Harry Vigors (5) takes off valuable weight, which may be the key factor if she can settle close enough to the pace.|

runners_data.name: Graniteville
runners_data.note: Marco Botti's filly returns after only nine days, having run four times this season for a modest form line of 0-464 including a 10th over 6f on Soft — the step up to 1m on Good is a logical switch, but her overall profile in this grade reads as one to beat rather than to follow, with Benoit de la Sayette doing well to find a clear passage from a small field.|

runners_data.name: Sydney Rock
runners_data.note: Oliver Cole's filly shows three placings from eight starts and is a genuine hold-up horse by style — the redistribution to midfield on the map is a consequence of the field structure, not her natural preference, meaning she will need a stronger gallop than Withtearsinmyeyes is likely to serve up if she is to land a telling late blow.|

runners_data.name: Withtearsinmyeyes
runners_data.note: The race's sole front-runner for Jack Channon and David Probert, she carries four consecutive placed runs including two runner-up efforts over this trip on Good and Standard — uncontested lead position in a five-runner maiden is exactly the scenario that suits her profile and the 9-day turnaround suggests she is in form and ready.|

runners_data.name: Zupa Trupa
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's filly reappears after 261 days off having shown only a fourth on debut over 7f at Sandown — lightly raced with an OR of 120 that matches Esplanade and hints at unrealised potential, and Beckett's strong record with patient, lightly-raced fillies makes her the main wildcard despite the long layoff and Rhys Clutterbuck's inexperience at this level.|

races.paceDynamic: Withtearsinmyeyes is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-runner field and, with no rival likely to contest her for the lead, she should settle into an uncontested, unhurried gallop around the Ffos Las mile on Good ground. That controlled, sustainable tempo means the race will be run to her timetable from the outset, with Esplanade, Graniteville, and Sydney Rock all tracking from off the pace and Zupa Trupa's positioning uncertain given her lightly-raced profile. The absence of any genuine pace pressure makes this a set-piece for Withtearsinmyeyes to control the race entirely from the front, dictating the fractions and kicking when she chooses — a profile that strongly favours the front-runner and any prominent closer capable of tracking and matching that move in the straight, rather than true hold-up horses needing a strong gallop to close into. Note that this field contains more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear; Sydney Rock is a genuine hold-up horse whose note flags redistribution to midfield, meaning it will not naturally secure even that drawn position freely.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Withtearsinmyeyes Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Withtearsinmyeyes bowls off in front, sets a measured tempo, and kicks decisively entering the straight.
scenarios.body: With no rival willing or able to match her early, she dictates fractions, keeps the race at a gallop that suits her stamina, and the honest placed form (2232) shows she handles Good ground over this trip well enough to hold on. A front-runner left alone on Good ground at Ffos Las over a flat mile has every structural advantage in a small maiden field.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Closer Gets The Kick
scenarios.trigger: If Withtearsinmyeyes sets a slightly too-strong early pace and one prominent-tracking rival pounces in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A runner able to sit a length or two off the leader and inherit momentum into the straight would benefit most here, with Esplanade — the highest-rated runner on OR=120 — best positioned as a hold-up type who could slot into a prominent berth in a small field. The class edge for Esplanade over these rivals could tell late if the pace was slightly more generous than Withtearsinmyeyes intended.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Debutante Zupa Trupa Blindsides
scenarios.trigger: If Zupa Trupa, with Ralph Beckett's fine record with lightly-raced fillies and 261 days off, shows significant improvement on her sole run and quickens past a conservative leader.
scenarios.body: Beckett runners returning from long absences in maidens at this level command respect, and OR=120 alongside Esplanade suggests there is talent here that one run barely exposed. If she settles kindly under Clutterbuck and produces a sprint in the straight, the unconvincing pace scenario could be the ideal soft landing for a filly with raw ability.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Sydney Rock Delivers Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and Sydney Rock, a genuine hold-up horse, gets a clear run late.
scenarios.body: Sydney Rock's redistribution from true hold-up to mapped midfield flags the structural problem: a genuinely modest pace set by Withtearsinmyeyes is unlikely to generate the end-to-end gallop this profile needs to close ground. The STYLE_FIT discount of 0.92 and the reality of a controlled small-field mile mean this scenario depends on conditions that simply will not materialise as forecast.

watchPoints.text: Withtearsinmyeyes — watch whether David Probert sends her straight to the front or is momentarily checked; if she bowls off uncontested the whole pace map locks in, but any early traffic from a five-runner break could disrupt her rhythm.|

Zupa Trupa — 261 days off for a Beckett OR=120 filly is a serious angle; if she shows natural pace in the paddock and travels well early in the race, her unchallenged form profile could be hiding genuine ability.|

Esplanade — Harry Vigors's 5lb claim is meaningful at this level; watch whether she can slot in a tracking position rather than settling deep, because her hold-up style in a slowly-run race leaves her vulnerable to the leader kicking and going clear.|

Sydney Rock — as the redistributed horse mapped to midfield rather than her natural rear position, watch whether Mason Paetel attempts to push her forward early to compensate, which would alter the pace equation slightly and benefit the true closers.|

Going confirmation — all races on the card are returning Good, and Ffos Las's flat track tends to ride consistent throughout the day; if any softening is reported by the time this race runs, Graniteville's Soft-going efforts become slightly more relevant.|

races.name: Thomas Arms Llanelli Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Belltony
runners_data.note: Modest record on similar going (2 places from 5 runs), winless in 5 outings, 59 days off — a genuine hold-up performer who will be bundled into midfield rather than racing from the rear where it operates best, which further compromises a limited profile.
runners_data.comment: Belltony catches the eye as the top-rated runner in this field, and he has experience of both today's trip and conditions; the concern is that he has been winless in his last five starts and returns after 59 days off.

runners_data.name: Dinah Myte
runners_data.note: John Gallagher's yard is 1 from 6 in the last 14 days and this 4-year-old has placed twice over 10f on Good, but at 1m she drops a touch short of her best trips; though a natural hold-up horse, she'll be pressed into a mid-pack slot rather than finding daylight at the back.
runners_data.comment: Ranked last on our figures and carrying a hefty 135 lb, Dinah Myte faces a stiff task, and a sixth-place finish last time out does little to inspire confidence, though she has run over today's trip and going before and does own a win in her last six starts.

runners_data.name: Eye Of The Water
runners_data.note: The race-shaper: lone confirmed front-runner with headgear, 58 days off, 10 years old but consistent at 8f on Good (4 places from 15 similar-going runs); if the energy levels hold into the straight this is the horse whose tactical dominance defines the entire race shape.
runners_data.comment: Eye Of The Water has shown a knack for hitting the frame, finishing third two of his last three outings, and he has experience over today's trip and conditions — yet to score in recent starts, and 58 days off the track is the question he must answer here.

runners_data.name: King Of The Dance
runners_data.note: Lightly raced recently (7 days ago, blinkers on), with three places from eight Good-ground starts and a second over this trip; naturally tracks the leader and is ideally suited to a race with one front-runner and a moderate tempo — his profile fits Scenario A and B best.
runners_data.comment: Third three starts back and runner-up five starts back, King Of The Dance brings solid recent placing form into this, and at just seven days since his last start he arrives fit and ready; has run over today's trip and going, and 135 lb from stall five is a workable enough ask for a gelding yet to score in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Launceston
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's yard active (3/37 in 14 days) and this 4-year-old has place form over 8-10f on Good, but a natural hold-up runner whose preferred deep position is denied by the volume of closers — Myla Coppins (5) claiming 5lbs adds appeal but can't overcome the positional squeeze.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Launceston faces a stiff task ranked eighth of ten on our figures, and a 46-day absence adds to the concern; he has run over today's trip and going, and a career-best effort in recent starts would be needed.

runners_data.name: Pebble Dash
runners_data.note: David Probert aboard gives confidence, and the horse has placed at 8f on Going-to-Standard, but four consecutive fourths and a third suggest a horse that runs its race without winning it; though a genuine hold-up type, it will be sitting in midfield traffic rather than finding the clear passage it needs.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked ninth of ten on our figures, Pebble Dash is hard to fancy, though he does return after 34 days and has run over today's trip and going before; a third last time out at least suggests he retains some ability.

runners_data.name: Private Officer
runners_data.note: 303 days off is a significant query and the last two runs produced a 0 and a dash — yet has a win on Good over this distance and Adrian Wintle's horses can return fresh; the long layoff is the dominant concern but the profile is live if fit.
runners_data.comment: Private Officer showed a winning turn of foot when landing the spoils three starts back, and his experience over today's trip and going is a clear asset carrying 135 lb from stall 2; the main concern is a lengthy 303-day absence.

runners_data.name: West Hill Rosie
runners_data.note: Jeff Mullins sends this 4-year-old out 23 days after a sixth, with a place at 10f on Good already on the board; naturally holds up but not redistributed, suggesting she can track from the rear legitimately — needs the race to be truly run to deliver her finishing effort.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, West Hill Rosie does have experience over today's trip and shaped with some promise when third two starts back, though a sixth last time out suggests she faces a stiff task from stall six carrying 135 lb off an official mark of 50.

runners_data.name: Alice's Influence
runners_data.note: David Evans filly with visor fitted, one win and four places from 11 Good-ground runs over 8f — genuine course-and-distance form; though a true hold-up type, she's mapped into midfield given the field's composition, which slightly blunts her ability to produce her characteristic late surge.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in her last six starts, Alice's Influence does bring distance and going experience to the table, and 16 days since her last run suggests she arrives fresh; third and second efforts in recent starts hint at ability, though a career-best finish remains elusive.

runners_data.name: Castlekeely
runners_data.note: James Owen yard in form (5/48 in 14 days) and this 3-year-old was second at 8f on Good last time out, but subsequent runs have been poor; a hold-up horse pushed into midfield by field composition, and recent form figures of 0-8-7-0-2 suggest inconsistency rather than a reliable threat.
runners_data.comment: Castlekeely showed his best recent form when second last time out, and has run over today's trip and going before, but he carries 129 lb from stall nine and has been winless in his last five starts, leaving him with plenty to prove against stronger company.

races.paceDynamic: Eye Of The Water is the sole confirmed front-runner and, at 10 years old with a habit of going prominent (headgear noted), will stride to the front from the off and attempt to control tempo over this flat Ffos Las mile on Good ground. With no other horse willing or able to press from outside, the pace is likely to be honest but sustainable rather than scorching — a single-digit field of hold-up horses behind a lone leader on a fair surface typically produces a well-strung-out race where the early gallop is just brisk enough to reward those who can travel mid-pack and deliver a finishing effort. This shape — a steady-to-fair solo lead, no pressure, moderate tempo — most clearly suits horses who can sit handy in second or third and kick off the back of the leader, rather than true closers needing a strong pace to close ground. This field is saturated with hold-up types: Castlekeely, Alice's Influence, Dinah Myte, Belltony, Launceston and Pebble Dash are all genuine back-of-the-field horses who are unlikely to get their natural position and will be shuffled into a congested midfield, making their tasks harder rather than easier.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Eye Of The Water Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Eye Of The Water dictates an unchallenged, measured tempo and the hold-up pack never gets a clear run at the final turn.
scenarios.body: Eye Of The Water sets a fractions-controlled gallop and kicks on entering the straight, exploiting the lack of any early challenger to build a lead that the hold-up midfield cluster — never finding clear daylight — cannot claw back; King Of The Dance, best placed to track from second or third, is ideally positioned to respond.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Handy Mover Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just honest enough that a horse travelling prominently in second or third coasts into the straight and outkicks the leader.
scenarios.body: King Of The Dance, who has been placed over this exact trip and surface combination repeatedly, is the archetype: sitting a length or two off Eye Of The Water, switching out at the two-furlong pole, and finding enough to get past; West Hill Rosie has placed at this trip on Good and carries the same tactical profile.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Storm Late
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is strong enough — perhaps if Castlekeely or Alice's Influence push forward early — to set up a truly run-on finish for the back markers.
scenarios.body: Alice's Influence has placed four times from six on similar going and, despite being redistributed forward on the map, is a genuine hold-up performer who would relish a true pace; Dinah Myte similarly has placed twice at this trip on Good and could pick them off if the field strings out.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Eye Of The Water sets a false pace, stops to nothing in the straight, and a scrimmaging finish among the congested midfield produces a shock result.
scenarios.body: With nine hold-up horses crammed into a narrow band of track behind a stopping leader, the race devolves into a traffic lottery; Private Officer, who has won over this distance on Good and returns from 303 days off with a fitness question mark but tactical freshness, or Pebble Dash could thread through.

watchPoints.text: Eye Of The Water — watch for whether Callum Hutchinson allows the horse to stride clear unchallenged or is asked to set a genuinely contested pace; if the leader bowls along without pressure the race is effectively run to its pattern from the first furlong.

King Of The Dance — watch its position out of the stalls: if Donagh Murphy (7lb claim) gets the horse to sit second or third immediately, it is in the ideal slot; if it gets shuffled back into the mid-pack cluster it loses its primary tactical advantage.

Alice's Influence and Castlekeely — both redistibuted hold-up types who may attempt to push forward to reclaim their natural position in the first two furlongs, which would inject unexpected early pace and dramatically alter the tempo assumptions.

Private Officer — 303 days off makes it essential to watch the paddock and market move; if it drifts in the betting it is likely returning short of full fitness, which would eliminate it from contention regardless of its theoretical form.

Pebble Dash — David Probert is a high-quality booking for an OR=47 horse in a low-grade classified stakes; watch whether the market reflects stable confidence, as the jockey booking is the only standout angle for a horse that has otherwise failed to convert its place form.

races.name: K P Tyres Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Seraglio Point
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who will press for the lead; good-ground form is modest (0W1P in two similar-going runs) and stepping up from 10f — likely to set the gallop but find the stamina test against him late.|
runners_data.comment: Seraglio Point shaped with promise when third two starts back, has run over today's trip and going, and his rating of 67 ranks him second in this field — the risk is that he has been winless in recent starts and must bounce back from an unplaced effort last time.

runners_data.name: Sunshine And Roses
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly with two recent placed efforts, including a win on softer ground at 8f, now stepping up to 1m2f which should suit her staying profile; Rose Dawes claims 5lb, and the Jack Channon yard is 1/18 in the past 14 days — needs the pace to truly collapse.|
runners_data.comment: Sunshine And Roses arrives in fine fettle just ten days since her last start, boasting a second last time out and a win three starts back, and she has experience over today's trip and conditions; the main risk is whether 135 lb from stall 11 blunts her finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Katalyst
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with a second placing over 9f on good ground and consistent midfield finishes at this sort of trip; Ryan Kavanagh claims 3lb, hood fitted, and while placed five times without winning, the step up to 1m2f on good ground is in his favour.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Katalyst does at least step back up having finished second three starts back, and she has run over today's trip and going before; a seventh last time out, however, means she must bounce back sharply from stall seven carrying 134 lb.

runners_data.name: Beryl's Girl
runners_data.note: Naturally prominent racer who has a win over 10f on good ground and runs with a hood to maintain focus; Callum Hutchinson rides and the yard is 1/29 in 14 days — the tactical position just off a strong pace gives her a live chance if she travels into it.|
runners_data.comment: Beryl's Girl won three starts back but has posted a seventh and a fourth since, and with her trainer in poor recent form — just one winner from 29 runners in the last fortnight — confidence is limited, even if she has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Grindleton
runners_data.note: Second confirmed front-runner who brings 12f placed form on good ground; Ebrahim Nader rides and the yard has been quiet (0/11), but Grindleton will be involved shaping the early tempo whether connections like it or not — likely to pay a price late.|
runners_data.comment: Grindleton arrives here in fine fettle just 24 days after finishing second last time out, and was second three starts back too, giving him strong claims as the top-rated runner in the field; he has experience over today's trip and going, though a win has so far eluded him in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Lc Tiffen
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse by nature with a win over 10f on good ground — mapped to midfield here purely because the field's rear is congested with true closers; Molly Gunn claims 5lb and the trainer is 1/3 in the past 14 days, giving a current form angle to monitor.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom two on our figures and carrying 132 lb from stall eight, Lc Tiffen is hard to fancy despite her win last time out; she has experience of today's distance and going, but her inconsistent recent record leaves her tough to trust.

runners_data.name: Thai Princess
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up type whose form is all at shorter trips (6-8f), making the step to 1m2f a significant query; Finley Marsh rides and she has only one good-ground run in her record (0W0P) — distance and ground stamina are the double concern.|
runners_data.comment: Thai Princess arrives here 44 days fresher, has run over today's trip, and our rating of 62 puts her firmly in contention from stall 3, with that third last time out the most encouraging recent signal — the risk is she remains winless in her last five starts.

runners_data.name: Pangbourne
runners_data.note: Consistent placer at 10-12f on good and soft, held in as a true hold-up horse whose ideal position at the rear may be crowded out today; Roger Teal yard is active (3/14), 14 days since last run, and good-ground form shows placed efforts — rate as a competitive deeper finisher if she gets a clear run.|
runners_data.comment: Pangbourne has shown consistency without a win in recent starts, her two runner-up efforts offset by a string of fifths, and 14 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh; experience over today's trip helps, but an official mark of 56 and ranking eighth of eleven point to a midfield ceiling.

runners_data.name: Give Me Sun
runners_data.note: The most credible of the three front-runners, owning a win over 10f on good ground and recent top-three placings at this trip; Benoit de la Sayette is an accomplished jockey — if any of the pace-setters is capable of controlling this race rather than combusting, Give Me Sun is the one.|
runners_data.comment: Winner last time out and placed twice in her last five starts, Give Me Sun arrives with solid recent form, though her official rating of 56 and a tough 131 lb burden may test her resolve; she has run over today's trip and going before and draws stall five.

runners_data.name: Ivat Ghia
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse with back-to-back second-place finishes on good ground at 8f, now going a quarter-mile further; Tyler Heard rides and the horse carries headgear — natural closer who will sit deep but faces the same spatial congestion at the rear as the other redistributed types.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with two successive runner-up finishes offering some consolation, Ivat Ghia nevertheless ranks ninth of eleven on our figures and faces a stiff ask from stall nine carrying 126 lb, making her hard to fancy despite the going experience.

runners_data.name: Summer Oasis
runners_data.note: Lowest-rated runner (OR 47) with a pattern of fading finishes flagged in the notes; Harry Vigors claims 5lb, and form figures of 8-9-11-9-6 at shorter trips on soft and firm do not inspire confidence stepping into this company over 1m2f — the redistribution out of a true hold-up berth only compounds the concern.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked bottom of this field on our figures, Summer Oasis faces a stiff ask, though 36 days since her last run leaves her fresh and stall four is a neutral enough pitch from which to try to reverse a run of poor form.

races.paceDynamic: Seraglio Point, Grindleton, and Give Me Sun are all confirmed front-runners, ensuring a strong, contested gallop from the outset over 1m2f on good ground at Ffos Las — a flat, fair track that will not allow the pace to be soft-pedalled. Three horses fighting for the lead will almost certainly produce a truly-run, stamina-testing affair where the early tempo is genuine and the race is likely to be strung out before halfway. This race shape strongly favours hold-up and late-finishing profiles, as the pace-setters are likely to burn each other off and leave the door open for closers to sweep through in the final two furlongs. However, the field contains more genuine hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear — Lc Tiffen, Pangbourne, and Ivat Ghia are all true hold-up horses who are redistributed into midfield positions because the map is saturated; of the three, Lc Tiffen, with a recent good-ground win, is best placed to secure a functional position just off the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners burn each other out and the race develops into a true stamina test in the final quarter-mile.
scenarios.body: Seraglio Point, Grindleton, and Give Me Sun press each other relentlessly, ensuring the field runs on empty entering the straight, leaving the genuine hold-up and midfield horses to pick up the pieces. Horses with proven stamina and good-ground form who have been covered up will be ideally positioned to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Pace-Setter Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three front-runners — most likely Give Me Sun, with a win over the trip — settles fractionally better and controls the race from a lenient lead.
scenarios.body: With the other pace-setters failing to sustain their challenge past halfway, the dominant lead horse dictates a strong but not suicidal tempo and proves tough enough to hold on. Give Me Sun's recent win at 10f on good ground and top-three consistency makes this the most credible individual pace scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Stayer Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent racer with stamina, particularly Beryl's Girl, travels sweetly just behind the pace and times a challenge to perfection in the straight.
scenarios.body: Beryl's Girl has a win over 10f on good ground, runs from a prominent position naturally, and wears a hood to aid focus — in a race where true hold-up horses may not get back as far as they want, tracking the pace from second or third could be the premium position. Her Eve Johnson Houghton trainer form of 1/29 is slim but the in-form yard note and good-ground win over course distance give her tactical relevance here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Fail To Reach
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves only moderate in practice — perhaps Grindleton or Seraglio Point drops back early — and the field compresses, leaving true hold-up types with no run.
scenarios.body: A compressed, slowly-developing race would strand the redistributed hold-up horses (Lc Tiffen, Ivat Ghia, Pangbourne) too far back with no gap to exploit, handing the race to a horse that can quicken from midfield rather than the rear. This scenario is discounted significantly because three confirmed front-runners make a truly-run race overwhelmingly probable.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Give Me Sun, Seraglio Point, and Grindleton engage in a genuine three-way duel for the lead exiting the first bend — if all three press hard, the tempo will be severe and the race could be decided in the final furlong by a closer.|

Lc Tiffen and Pangbourne are true hold-up horses redistributed into midfield; if the field compresses or gaps don't open in the straight, their routes to the front could be blocked, significantly reducing their effectiveness.|

Beryl's Girl is the key prominent tracker to watch — if she settles comfortably in second or third without being dragged into the pace battle, her 10f good-ground winning form makes her dangerous entering the straight.|

Thai Princess is stepping up sharply in trip from a maximum of 8f and has only one good-ground run in her profile — monitor for any signs of distress or loss of position mid-race as the stamina question becomes answered in real time.|

Summer Oasis carries the lowest rating and a fading-finish flag; if she is outpaced and loses contact before halfway, watch for Ivat Ghia, mapped nearby, to be similarly caught in traffic with nowhere to travel.|

races.name: Noah's Ark Christmas Party Race Day Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Hibernate
runners_data.note: The race's lone genuine pace-setter, Hibernate has won twice at 12f on Good ground and faces a light enough claimer in Mason Paetel; OR 70 gives it a workable mark but the STYLE_FIT flag suggests tempering expectations if it meets more pace than anticipated — here it won't, so the tactical advantage is real.
runners_data.comment: Ran to a second two starts back and has winning form in recent starts, so the ability is there, but a fourth last time out and a 37-day absence leave questions; has run over today's trip and going, and 135 lb is no featherweight at a rating of 70.

runners_data.name: Crackergee
runners_data.note: David Probert takes over on a horse whose only win in recent form came on Soft at 12f; the move back to 14f matches its stamina profile but Good ground and no wins at all on similar going (0W0P in 13 sim-going runs) is a factual concern, and it will need a proper gallop to deliver from the hold-up berth.
runners_data.comment: Crackergee landed a win two starts back and has run over today's trip, giving him a solid platform to threaten here off a mark of 70, though that fifth last time out after a 46-day absence raises a question over his sharpness returning to action.

runners_data.name: Robusto
runners_data.note: Won at 12f on Good last time out for Eve Johnson Houghton (1 winner from 29 in the last 14 days) and has back-to-back Good-ground placed efforts at the trip; headgear (blinkers) applied, 19 days fresh, and a prominent style that suits a race where Hibernate controls the pace — the profile fits the dominant scenario well.
runners_data.comment: Robusto won last time out and was third two starts back, giving him strong recent form credentials, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions; a struggling trainer yard is the one reservation, but his profile marks him out as the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Raintown
runners_data.note: Consistent placer whose form string (342312) is tidy and who has won at 10f on Good; the hood is on again and Taylor Fisher takes over — but five of the last five runs are over 10-11f, so this 14f trip is an open stamina question even if the going is ideal.
runners_data.comment: Raintown arrives in solid nick, second last time out and a winner two starts back, with experience over today's trip and going and a lively rating to support his claims; the chief concern is whether 133 lb blunts his finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Flightofthephoenix
runners_data.note: Career wins have come on Soft/Standard and the best recent form (a win and a second) was on cut or artificial surfaces; though its true style is hold-up, this horse is pushed into midfield by the preponderance of hold-up types in the field and the STYLE_FIT flag warrants discounting its chance in a shape that doesn't deliver the patient, late-running race it needs.
runners_data.comment: Flightofthephoenix won last time out and was second two starts back, but her two seventh-placed efforts three and four starts ago temper expectations; she has going experience to call on and arrives fresh enough at 18 days, though 133 lb is a significant weight to shoulder.

runners_data.name: King's Castle
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old with strong course-form (4 wins, 8 places in 15 similar-going runs) and David Simcock sends it out having had no runners strike in the last 14 days; prominent style sits perfectly behind Hibernate and the consistency record at 12f on Good is the best in the field, though a step to 14f is worth watching.
runners_data.comment: Consistently in the mix — King's Castle has finished third or better in three of his last five starts and returns here in good order after 22 days, with experience of today's trip and conditions; the concern is he remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Luan
runners_data.note: Carries a tongue-tie and is partnered by Benoit de la Sayette; form figures of 1-1 in the recent past are intriguing but both wins came on Standard/AW, and on Good turf the record is 13th last time out — its hold-up style is squeezed forward by the map redistribution, which sits poorly given it needs to come from well off the pace to be effective.
runners_data.comment: Two wins in his last five starts show Luan has ability on a good day, and he has run over today's trip before, but finishing ninth last time out and ranking last on our figures makes him very hard to fancy here.

runners_data.name: Shaffron
runners_data.note: 106 days since last run is the longest layoff in the field and David Menuisier has had no winners from five runners in the past 14 days; a natural hold-up horse that has been placed into midfield against its preferred style — the combination of the long break, no win on Good or Good-ish turf in recent history, and the style displacement makes this a difficult proposition.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and absent for 106 days, Shaffron is hard to fancy from seventh in the rankings, though she has run over today's distance and going before, and her third last time out offers a sliver of encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: Hibernate is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival likely to push hard for the lead from the outset, should control proceedings at a measured gallop on Good ground over 1m4f at Ffos Las. Robusto and King's Castle will track in behind from their prominent positions, creating a compact lead group while the remainder string out through midfield and behind. This unhurried, single-file shape suits horses who can sit close to a controlled pace and produce a sustained finish rather than a sharp late burst — making the prominent and close-tracking profiles the primary beneficiaries. It is worth noting that Flightofthephoenix, Luan, and Shaffron are genuine hold-up types displaced into midfield on the map because the field holds more rear-running horses than the race shape can naturally accommodate, meaning they are unlikely to operate from as far back as they ideally want, further compressing the middle order and adding bodies near the pace without any of them truly dictating it.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hibernate Controls, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Hibernate dictates a smooth, uncontested gallop and the closers cannot sustain a winning run from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Hibernate sets a fair tempo with Robusto and King's Castle sitting just behind, and the race unfolds in a line with the principals having their chance turning in; the prominent pair have the tactical position to challenge without burning energy chasing, making this the dominant scenario on Good ground at this trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Honest, Closers Reel In
scenarios.trigger: If Hibernate's gallop is slightly stronger than anticipated and opens the race up for hold-up horses to finish powerfully.
scenarios.body: Raintown, who has consistent form at the track across shorter trips and wears a hood, could find this distance on the slow side but benefits if a genuine pace is set; Crackergee from the hold-up berth is a bigger price hope if conditions suit a late sweep.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent War, Front Runs Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Hibernate meets no serious challenge and the gaps never close in a race run at a very steady tempo.
scenarios.body: With a stranglehold on the front and jockey Mason Paetel (3lb claimer) able to coast without pressure, Hibernate could simply outsprint rivals who are caught flat-footed behind a muddling gallop; Robusto is best placed of the chasers given recent course-and-distance winning form.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If pace collapses completely and genuine hold-up types — despite their redistribution — produce a finishing burst from the rear.
scenarios.body: This scenario is the least likely because Flightofthephoenix, Luan, and Shaffron are all true hold-up horses mapped forward against their will and are unlikely to secure the wide, late-running position they need; even if one finds a gap, their style-fit tags reduce confidence in them executing from an unfamiliar position.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Robusto pushes forward to sit second behind Hibernate at the start — if Harry Vigors (5lb) settles it close to the pace, it holds the ideal tactical position and becomes the most dangerous challenger turning in.

King's Castle's stamina at 14f is unproven in this form cycle despite strong course form; if the pace is truly modest and the race becomes a sprint, its age (9) and the extra two furlongs over its recent trips could expose it late.

Raintown's hood and front-running connections (T14: 2/16) suggest it may be ridden more aggressively than its hold-up tag implies — if it disputes the early pace with Hibernate it could compromise its own stamina over a trip it has not convincingly stayed.

Luan and Shaffron are both displaced hold-up types who will struggle to find space at the rear in a compressed, single-file race; if either is checked or forced wide on the bend at Ffos Las, their already-limited winning chance effectively disappears.
Crackergee has had 46 days off and has zero wins or places on similar going from 13 attempts — David Probert will need an unusually messy race at the front to get involved from the hold-up berth.
